newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dollar corralled, seeks greener pastures.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dollar corralled, seeks greener pastures.

text.p: The dollar remained largely rangebound and a bit on the defensive Thursday, with modest consolidative selling seen necessary before the greenback can resume its upward climb, technical analysts said.
The overnight decline below 1.73 marks and continuing erosion toward 1.72 in U.S. trade left the dollar in a precarious short-term position, chartists said.

"It's not constructive that the dollar is failing to get above 1.73 (marks) and we may be building a bit of a top," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at IDEA. "These are not the levels where you necessarily want to go long dollar/mark."

Dollar/mark seems at least a few sessions away from retesting 1.74, a high dating back to February 1994. On the way up, the greenback will meet resistance at 1.7330 and 1.7370 marks, technicians said.
"I think the dollar is going to form a base here and have a blowoff rally. The question is, from what level," said Johsnon.
The dollar got as high as 1.7375 marks early this week but sank sharply amid reported profit-taking. Sideways trade should yield to a fresh rally in coming sessions, Morden said.
"Dollar/mark sentiment is still very bullish," he said.
While the mark/yen recovery has reined in dollar/mark, it shored up a flagging dollar/yen, chartists noted.
The greenback slipped as low as 125.10 yen overnight before catching a bid and returning to the 126 area.
"Mark/yen and dollar/yen found a base and we had a subsequent rally," said Morden. "We still have to stick with the view that dollar/yen looks bullish."
Morden cited support at 125 yen, which he called a 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the dollar's rise to 127.19 on April 10 from a low of 121.35 on April 1.
